The refined operator registered in Palomar

PALOMAR-2026-08-27-000018 v3 registers one selected declaration:

CollatzEndpointTransportPalomar.quantitative_arbitrary_target_endpoint_transport

It states refined arbitrary-target endpoint transport with a density exponent linear in the incoming exponent and the sublinear prefactor in the current manuscript. The record fixes Lean 4.33.0 and source commit 9505e8fd59f2b49a2dad269436766319c57b4012.

Read the exact statement in Challenge.lean and the proof adapter in Solution.lean. The registry records the dependency pins, Comparator and NanoDa replay, and permitted standard axioms.

Relation to the manuscript and earlier formalization

The manuscript's public operator release is tagged v2.2.0, at 6e4d0d4982cdc321d03c3e467704a4b89681afee, with software archive 10.5281/zenodo.22544010. The later registered commit above is its own immutable source identity.

The earlier CET v2.0.1 package formalizes the preceding separate descent, exceptional-count and timed conclusions. Those earlier roots should not be described as registration of every strengthened joint application in manuscript v2.2.0. Section 8.2 of the full paper gives the correspondence and evidence status of each component.

Earlier article v2.0.3 theorem map.

Paper, code and citation

An arbitrary-target Collatz endpoint-transport theorem with a refined prefactor, and a quantitative natural-density descent application for every delta below 0.251245530155874.
